resources.string: ProxyFlow sends your apps\' TCP connections through a proxy you already have: one from a provider you pay, or a server of your own.
An HTTP proxy that allows tunnels (CONNECT), or a SOCKS5 proxy
Its username and password, if it has one
ProxyFlow doesn\'t sell or provide proxies. It\'s free, needs no account and has no servers of its own: your profiles stay on this phone.
Your apps → ProxyFlow → your proxy → the internet
Your apps\' connections go to ProxyFlow, then to your proxy, then to the internet.
Through your proxy, so usually unreachable
Blocked traffic is never sent around your proxy. Video calls usually switch to TCP; apps that can\'t won\'t work while connected. Ping isn\'t answered.
Your proxy provider can see which sites you connect to and any unencrypted data. Choose one you trust.

To send apps\' traffic to your proxy, ProxyFlow uses Android\'s VPN feature. The first time you connect, Android asks you to allow it. There is no VPN server: traffic goes from this phone to your proxy. While connected, Android shows a key icon, and only one VPN app can be on at a time.
Some of Android\'s own traffic, apps in a work profile and tethered devices don\'t use the VPN. About & privacy has the details.
A notification shows whether your traffic is going through your proxy and lets you disconnect in one tap. You can change this later in Settings.
